title: Day 27 — Circuit Breaker for a Flaky Client
prompt: This circuit breaker wraps a flaky client. It trips even when failures were separated by successes and never really recovers. Time is injected as `now`. How would you fix it?

clarifications.answer: A successful call must reset the failure count to 0 (close the breaker). That's the missing piece.
The threshold counts CONSECUTIVE failures — a success in between clears the count.
While open (now < openUntil) the breaker must throw CircuitOpenError WITHOUT calling fn.
Once the cooldown elapses (now >= openUntil) it's half-open: one trial call is allowed. Success closes it; failure re-opens it.
Time is passed in as `now` (ms), so tests are deterministic — no real clock.
Three states: closed, open, half-open. The bug is a missing transition on success.

hints: Sketch the three states and their transitions before touching code.
The bug: the success path returns the result but never resets this.failures to 0.
Add 'this.failures = 0;' before returning on success. Everything else (open check, threshold, cooldown) is already there.
